1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with clear hierarchy and comfortable line spacing, though letter spacing is conventional rather than notably generous.

2.why: Every instruction is a short sentence-case sentence with no italics or all-caps; the only uppercase text is the hex recovery codes and [SIMULATION] log tags, which are not instructions.

3.why: Only desktop-width screenshots are provided, and while the narrow single-column card would likely adapt to a phone, the monospace log text already wraps mid-word ('enrolmen t.') inside the card, so mobile readability cannot be confirmed.

4.why: Instructions are one or two short plain sentences (e.g., 'Generate backup codes and store them safely'), with only minor jargon such as 'manual Base32 secret'.

5.why: Email and mobile fields show pre-filled values and the test OTP appears in the logs, but the authenticator code field itself has no placeholder or format example at the point of entry.

6.why: Step 5 explicitly instructs the user to 'Enter the displayed six-digit test code from Logs', forcing them to scan a dense multi-line monospace log block to proceed.

7.why: The Base32 secret and all eight recovery codes are rendered as ordinary selectable text, so they can be selected and copied, although no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code, otpauth:// link, or any equivalent alternative to manual entry appears on any screen; the flow explicitly says 'Use this manual Base32 secret in an authenticator app'.

9.why: The forms use standard labelled inputs, but no autofill or password-manager behaviour can be verified from the screenshots, and the OTP field shows no one-time-code support hints.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the step and a single solid blue primary button, though the red 'Log out' button on the completion screen competes somewhat for attention.

11.why: Each step centres on one main action (sign in, confirm, create, verify, generate, save); secondary options like 'Regenerate codes' and 'Log out' are present but visually subordinate on most screens.

12.why: Only the final 'MFA is active' screen plainly states the outcome in green text; intermediate transitions show no explicit success message, with event confirmations appearing only in the [SIMULATION] logs.

13.why: A 'Regenerate codes' button and post-enrolment 'View recovery codes' access are provided with no visible penalty, although retrying a failed code entry and a hide option are not demonstrated.

14.why: No error message appears in any of the 13 screenshots, so their wording and tone cannot be assessed.

15.why: No countdown, timer, or time warning appears on any screen, and the test OTP remains static, indicating no imposed time pressure as far as can be observed.
